clue.text: Thief went in for stock-raising ?

parts.note: stock-raising usually means breeding farm animals, but read literally it is raising (lifting, stealing) livestock, which is what a rustler does

explanation.surface: A thief who gave up crime and took up farming livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock-raising' looks like breeding animals; here 'raising' means lifting in the slang sense of stealing, so the thief raises stock by making off with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals livestock, and to 'lift' is slang for to steal, so a rustler is a lifter of herds.

clue.text: Allied officer replaced agent

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of the word that follows are put back in another order

explanation.surface: An Allied commander was replaced by a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related or kindred, sharing a common origin.

clue.text: Characteristic knack, going up it

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: art means a skill or knack

explanation.surface: A typical knack is rising to the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing quality or feature of someone.

clue.text: Was relieved to find a female worker ?

definitions.meaning: the South African town besieged by the Boers and relieved in 1900
a lady who is a smith, a metalworker

explanation.surface: Someone is glad to find that the worker is a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was relieved' reads as feeling better; it is the town whose relief from siege in 1900 was a famous event of the Boer War.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Natal was famously relieved after a long siege; a woman blacksmith would be a lady metalworker.

clue.text: A one thousand pound distribution of capital

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

indicators.note: a distribution spreads the letters out, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A thousand-pound payout of capital funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution of capital' looks like finance; 'distribution of' rearranges A, I and M (one and a thousand in Roman numerals), with L for pound in front. 'capital' is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Running away clutching article from the window

indicators.note: clutching means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: flight is the act of fleeing
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A thief flees holding an item from the window.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is a semicircular window above a door.

clue.text: She, gets one in besides

indicators.note: in says the letter for one goes inside the word for besides

parts.note: else means besides, in addition
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman gets one in as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a female given name, a woman as a 'she'.

clue.text: Bloomer awakens a sleeper in the form ?

parts.note: a hare's resting place is called its form, so a hare lies in the form
a bell, like an alarm, wakes someone sleeping

explanation.surface: A blunder wakes someone sleeping on a bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a blunder; it is a flower, something that blooms. A hare's form is its hollow in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The harebell is a blue bell-shaped wild flower, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Such hard-baked exteriors

parts.note: the hard outer layer of a loaf, baked firm in the oven

explanation.definitionFit: The browned outer layer of bread is baked hard while the inside stays soft.

clue.text: Soldier drugs a settler going to the island.

indicators.note: something that settles the letters of the words before it sorts them into a new order

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, is the crossword's usual island

explanation.surface: A soldier slips drugs to a settler bound for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settler' reads as a colonist but works as the anagram signal on DRUGS A, giving GUARDS; then MAN, the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Guards regiment is an infantry soldier of the household troops.

clue.text: A way to look for a step up

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
an air is a look or appearance, as in 'an air of calm'

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a way of seeing over something higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A way to look' wants to be one phrase meaning gaze, suggesting a sound-alike; it splits into street and a look in the sense of an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Each tread of a staircase is a single step that raises you higher.

clue.text: Would he urge us to invest in oils?

definitions.text: Would he urge us to invest in oils?

parts.words: Would he urge us to invest in oils?
parts.note: investing in oils sounds like buying shares in petroleum, but oils are also oil paints, which a painter works in

explanation.surface: A stockbroker wonders whether to recommend oil shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter works in oil paints, so would want everyone to take up oil painting.

clue.text: Keep list giving 'makers of cakes

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are what the cakes are made of, rearranged into them

explanation.surface: Bakers keep a list of the people who make the cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makers of' tells you the letters of KEEP LIST make up the cakes once rearranged. Pikelets are small thick pancakes, a kind of crumpet eaten in Britain and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikelet is a small griddle cake like a crumpet or drop scone.

clue.text: Girl gives back jolly good. fruit

indicators.note: giving back means the pieces that follow are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-rate, jolly good
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A girl returns some excellent fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives back' turns the whole run round, the rating for first-rate and the fruit together, rather than either piece alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Emilia is a female given name, as borne by Iago's wife in Othello.

clue.text: Opera composed by Noel — a hit, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters might be put together another way

explanation.surface: An opera written by Noel Coward might be a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed by' looks like the anagram signal but is a link; 'possibly' rearranges NOEL A HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, about a fairy and the House of Lords.

clue.text: A fellow with permits for headgear

parts.note: a chap is a man, a fellow
lets means allows or permits

explanation.surface: A man holding licences to sell hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or garland worn on the head.

clue.text: Soldier meets Sapper returning to ship

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, the corps whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: A soldier meets a military engineer going back to the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed private vessel licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Moral, instructions. Polonius '. gave Laertes

parts.note: in Hamlet Polonius sends his son off with rules of conduct such as 'neither a borrower nor a lender be'

explanation.definitionFit: Rules of conduct are commandments for behaviour, like the father's advice in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Fish returned to dock by firm

indicators.note: returned means the word for dock is written backwards

parts.note: to clip is to dock or cut short, as with a tail
hard means firm, solid

explanation.surface: A fish sent back to the harbour by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a harbour (and 'firm' like a company), but dock means cut short, CLIP, which 'returned' turns to PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, the adult sardine.

clue.text: Advertisement for a mail clerk ?

definitions.meaning: a bill or placard put up on a wall

explanation.surface: A job advertisement for a post-room clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed bill is stuck up to advertise; one who mails letters is someone who posts.

clue.text: Stops scores of overtaking drivers

definitions.meaning: in cricket a fielder stops the ball, so 'stops' as a verb means intercepts in the field
the runners in a motor race are its field, a large body of drivers

explanation.surface: Traffic halts dozens of drivers trying to pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a noun; it is the verb, as a fielder in cricket stops the ball. The second sense is the whole entry in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercept the ball in cricket is the verb's sense; a race's starters are collectively its runners and riders.

clue.text: Conductor said to be a man of 'some force

indicators.note: said to be means the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a sergeant is a rank in a police force

explanation.surface: A conductor is supposedly a powerful man.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a British orchestral conductor; his name is spoken like the police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Malcolm Sargent conducted the Proms for many years, an orchestra leader.

clue.text: Early snack in Kent

definitions.meaning: the snack takes its name from an earl (Earl-y), the Earl of ... who ate meat between bread at the gaming table
a town in Kent, the county of south-east England

explanation.surface: A snack eaten early in the day in a south-east English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' reads as 'in the morning' but hides 'Earl-y', of the Earl: the snack is named after the fourth Earl of Sandwich. Sandwich is also one of the old Cinque Ports in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread around a filling is named after the Earl who ate it, and a Kentish port shares the name.

clue.text: One 'of the things' for which a bride is taken

definitions.text: One 'of the things' for which a bride is taken

parts.words: One 'of the things' for which a bride is taken
parts.note: the wedding vow takes a spouse 'for better

explanation.definitionFit: The marriage service vow includes 'for better, for worse', so a bride is taken for the poorer outcome too.

clue.text: All hands to the pumps as he prepares for action ?

definitions.text: All hands to the pumps as he prepares for action ?

parts.words: All hands to the pumps as he prepares for action ?
parts.note: 'all hands to the pumps' is a call to bail out a ship, but pumps are also light shoes for the ballet, and a performer reaches for them before going on

explanation.surface: A crew rushes to the bilge pumps as their captain readies for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet performer pulls on light slippers before stepping out on stage.

clue.text: Alternative to one of 8 provides small comfort

definitions.meaning: the soft inside of bread as opposed to its hard outside, the answer to 8 down
as in 'a ... of comfort', a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A substitute for one hard thing gives little consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft inner bread is the opposite of the hard exterior, and a tiny morsel is a scrap of consolation.

clue.text: Chaldean trip?

parts.note: Ur was the city of the Chaldees, so a Chaldean trip would be a journey to that ancient city

explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey; split it and it says where in Chaldea you are going.

clue.text: Anaesthetic is one of two I omitted

indicators.note: omitted means the letter named is left out of the word

parts.note: either means one or the other of two

explanation.surface: Faced with two anaesthetics, the patient skips one.
explanation.definitionFit: Diethyl ether was an early general anaesthetic, breathed in to put patients under.

clue.text: Course of action for getting monthly return by river

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: return means the month's abbreviation is turned backwards

parts.note: DEC, short for December, is one of the months
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A plan of action for collecting a return each month beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monthly return' reads as a regular report; 'return' turns December's short form backwards. The Ure is a North Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established method or way of going about something.

clue.text: People take the underdone part of this dish, some say

parts.note: the Welsh are the people of Wales
rare means underdone (of meat), and a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Diners take the rare portion of a dish, so some claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' points to the dish's other name, Welsh rabbit, which some insist on. It is melted cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a savoury of melted seasoned cheese on toast.
